codeReview.summary: The feature fixes the immediate import blocker and adds recovery normalization coverage plus a dev harness, but it leaves a blocking mismatch in the booking-detail sign-in continuation path: unauthenticated detail pages still preserve `/bookings/[id]` directly instead of the canonical `/bookings/recover` entrypoint required for supported tokenized flows and later live entitled validation.

issues.description: The fix swaps alias imports for a deep relative path to `components/dashboard/*`. It unblocks the build, but it bypasses the repo's established alias convention and hard-codes a fragile five-level traversal that is easy to break on future moves.

When an unauthenticated guest opens `/bookings/[bookingId]` without an `sr_access` cookie, the page still redirects to `/auth/signin?redirectedFrom=/bookings/[bookingId]` instead of preserving the canonical recovery entrypoint for tokenized/manage links. Because the feature contract requires supported tokenized booking links to route through `/bookings/recover`, preserve safe continuation, and leave a deterministic entitled public booking path for later live validation, this direct sign-in handoff breaks the canonical continuation path once the token has been stripped from the final URL. A guest who lands on the final detail URL after recovery but loses the recovery cookie cannot recover back through `/bookings/recover` from the preserved intent.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The `guest-routing-worker` skill says to start from `.factory/library/guest-routes.md`, `.factory/library/environment.md`, and `.factory/library/user-testing.md`, but it does not tell workers what to do when a requested feature's first step is to repair a known baseline blocker before any RED test can run. This worker had to deviate and document that the failing baseline itself was the assigned blocker.

Future validators will otherwise discover the page but may not know why it only shows the missing-secret message.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared validation guidance notes the auth-validation and restaurants empty-state fixtures, but it does not document the new deterministic public booking harness path `/dev/booking-recovery` that this feature introduced for later live entitled booking-detail coverage.

summary: Review failed. The feature mostly implements the recovery normalization contract, but it leaves a blocking gap in continuation behavior: once a guest reaches the final token-free booking detail URL, the unauthenticated fallback still preserves `/bookings/[id]` directly instead of a canonical recovery route, so the recovery-based continuation contract is not fully maintained.
